title: Foundation executable specification
description: Objective: author development-only held-out models, fakes, fixtures, and fault schedules for J1, J3, J4, stale clients, and the linear effect boundary. Deliverable: packages/testkit/src/foundation and tests/fault/foundation with fixed fixture hashes and honest expected failures. NOT in scope: production implementation or confirmatory BENCH corpus bytes. Hard dependency: Runtime contract registry. Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/** and tests/fault/foundation/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/testkit typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/testkit test.
definitionOfDone: Fixtures and oracles are deterministic, versioned, hashed, and labeled DEVELOPMENT_ONLY and NOT_CONFIRMATORY.
Schedules cover stale version/lease, cancel-start, crash boundaries, zero-work false green, and honest UNKNOWN.
Missing production behavior fails with named stable outcomes rather than import or placeholder errors.
The focused testkit typecheck and test command exits 0 with expected-red fixtures mechanically distinguished.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

Assertions authored, all mutation-resistant (exact values, no truthiness):
1. Closed vocabulary: FOUNDATION_OUTCOME_KINDS === exactly [EXPECTED_RED, HONEST_UNKNOWN, PASS_EXPECTED, PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT].
2. Distinct artifact: version === "moe-foundation-expected-outcome/1"; the canonicalized manifest contains neither "moe-schedule-coverage/1" nor any "SCHEDULE_" substring, so no code or coverage authority is borrowed from the schedule-checker's source-derived universe.
3. One outcome per entry: entry ids unique, sorted, and equal to fixtureIds ∪ scheduleIds.
4. Partition completeness: union of the three journey partitions equals the manifest entry-id list exactly, plus per-journey size pins (FOUNDATION_PARTITION_COUNTS) so a dropped schedule cannot slip through silently.
5. Labels + pinned sha256 through the LANDED helpers only (identifyFoundationFixture wraps identifyCanonicalEvidence), and a volatility test: re-labelling a fixture with recordedAt/seed leaves the digest unchanged (schedule-model identity precedent).
6. Probe integrity in three directions — every ABSENT entry resolves to a declared probe AND every declared probe is claimed by an entry (no orphans either way); each probe reports absent on an unrelated export set; each probe goes RED when its named export appears; and pattern-bearing probes go RED on a differently-named export that still matches, which is the guard against ratchet rot when the eventual production name differs from my guess.
7. Determinism (two builds byte-identical via canonicalize + digest equality), zero BENCH-* identifiers in any foundation source or in the manifest, and held-out enforcement by source scan: no non-test .ts under packages/** may import anything matching foundation/.
8. Zero-work false-green oracle, both directions: an empty-diff/no-artifact/no-receipt/green-claiming trace must yield refusal J1_ZERO_WORK_FALSE_GREEN; a real-work trace with exactly three human actions must be accepted.

Design decision recorded for step 3-4 (keeps import discipline intact): the probe is a declarative spec (package name + absent export names + optional pattern) plus a pure evaluator over a caller-supplied export-name list. testkit never imports @moe/core or @moe/scheduler; the fault tests feed Object.keys of the real package namespaces into the same evaluator. foundation-fakes.ts — pure caller-driven ports, zero wall clock and zero randomness. createFixedClock consumes a caller-supplied instant list and THROWS on exhaustion rather than recycling the last value, because a schedule that reads more instants than it declared has changed shape and silently repeating would hide that. createRecordingDispatchPort throws on an undeclared command kind for the same reason: a schedule can never read a green it never declared. buildCommandEnvelopeRecord emits a record matching the landed RuntimeCommandEnvelope required/optional key sets exactly (verified against runtime-envelope.ts COMMAND_REQUIRED/COMMAND_OPTIONAL and the isHex64/isNonEmptyString/isSafeCount guards) with valid defaults, so a stale-client schedule states only the one field it is making hostile. encodeCanonicalBytes goes through the landed canonicalize, so identical records always produce identical bytes.

PROBE PATTERNS WERE COLLISION-CHECKED AGAINST THE LIVE EXPORT SETS, not guessed. I re-derived the runtime export names of @moe/core, @moe/store, @moe/scheduler and @moe/contracts after the mid-task core landing and confirmed none of "attempt", "dispatch", "acknowledg|^ack", "lease|fence", "release", "handoff", "claim", "timer", "review", "distribution" matches an already-exported runtime name. That matters twice over: a pattern that already matched would make the probe born-red, and a probe with only exact names rots silently when the surface eventually lands under a name nobody guessed. Note type-only exports erase at runtime, so Object.keys of the namespace is the right comparison set and e.g. the type AcceptanceClosureWitness does not collide.

Dropping a schedule from the catalogue breaks the pinned partition count in the spec test; dropping an executor breaks ownership; adding an entry with no executor breaks ownership too. THE RATCHET IS NOT TAUTOLOGICAL. produceAbsenceOutcome never echoes the declared outcome. It evaluates the probe against the LIVE Object.keys of the real package namespace and returns PASS_EXPECTED the moment the surface exists, so a landing surface turns the schedule red against its declared PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT and forces an honest manifest flip. Same for fixtures: outcomeFromVerdict runs the model and maps a refusal to EXPECTED_RED(refusalCode), so a model that stopped refusing would fail rather than agree with itself.

What actually EXECUTES today (no probe, real production code):
- J1 linear path through reduceProject register -> bind_repository -> activate (asserted READY), reduceGoal create (DRAFT) -> activate_initial_graph (EXECUTION_ENABLED), and the exact plan/initial-graph approval through reduceGraphRevision create -> submit (PENDING_APPROVAL) -> graph.approve (APPROVED).
- Cancel/start race arbitration: after goal.cancel the late start is refused ILLEGAL_TRANSITION with details.sourceState === "CANCELLED".
- J3 store crash boundaries against the landed SqliteEventStore: a commit whose second event reuses an existing event id throws DurableStoreError and leaves whole-or-none truth (version still 1, only evt-first present, and no receipt for the refused command id); a replayed command id returns disposition REPLAYED with the same event ids and does not double-write; a stale expectedVersion throws ExpectedVersionConflictError.
- J4 stale-client subset against the landed decoder and registry: a superseded schemaVersion is refused SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED carrying supportedSchemaVersion; a bad requestDigest / empty commandId / negative expectedVersion are refused INPUT_INVALID; a stale expectedVersion into reduceGoal is refused EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT with actualVersion and expectedVersion details.

LEASE STALENESS SPLIT HONESTLY rather than overclaimed: carriage and classification exist today and are asserted (a well-formed leaseAuthority decodes and preserves epoch 7, a malformed one is refused INPUT_INVALID, and STALE_LEASE/STALE_EPOCH are registered with httpStatus 412, DAEMON_VERIFIED truth, required detail keys exactly [expectedEpoch, observedEpoch], LEASE among validSources, RECONCILE / AFTER_REFRESH). Epoch ENFORCEMENT is what does not exist, and that is the one part carrying PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT behind probe:scheduler-authority-lease.

DEVIATION FROM THE STEP TEXT, stated rather than buried: the step said to reach lease staleness "against landed authority modules via ports". I did not deep-import packages/scheduler/src/authority/* from tests/. Those modules are landed but deliberately NOT exported from the scheduler package root, and packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts forbids that path shape everywhere it scans. tests/ happens to be outside its scan roots, so the import would have worked — but only by exploiting the gap, and it would have encoded a dependency on an unsupported internal path. Probing the supported root export set instead is both honest and falsifiable: the day authority is exported, the probe goes red and the schedule flips.

FIVE DEFECTS FOUND BY THE REVIEW AND FIXED BEFORE COMMIT:
1. Untested exported fakes. createFixedClock, createRecordingDispatchPort, createExportSurfacePort, buildCommandEnvelopeRecord and encodeCanonicalBytes were exported with no test — a reviewer would rightly ding that, and untested fakes are how a testkit lies. Added foundation-fakes.test.ts (108 lines) covering clock exhaustion, undeclared-dispatch-kind refusal, missing export surface, exact default envelope key set, conditional leaseAuthority, and canonical key ordering.
2. Scans with no floor. Both source scans would have passed trivially if they walked zero files — a fake gate. Pinned floors (>=7 foundation files, >=100 production files).
3. Held-out scan too narrow. It covered only packages/; extended to adapters/apps/packages (the scheduler boundary precedent) with an ENOENT guard so a missing adapters/ returns empty instead of throwing.
4. Import regex too narrow. It caught only `from "..."`, missing dynamic import() and require(). Broadened to all three forms.
5. node_modules skip was ineffective. `path.includes(sep + "node_modules" + sep)` never matches the node_modules directory itself (no trailing separator), so the walk descended one level into it. Changed to `entry.name === "node_modules"`.

Also turned two prose claims into live assertions: the three module KIND constants are asserted to equal DEVELOPMENT_ONLY/NOT_CONFIRMATORY, and the J1 fault test now asserts every member of J1_LINEAR_COMMAND_SEQUENCE is in RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS while goal.activate_initial_graph is NOT — pinning the vocabulary divergence I found at step 3 so nobody "fixes" it on a wrong assumption.

Checklist items considered and judged theoretical, recorded for QA rather than fixed: all foundation modules are pure functions over frozen data with no shared mutable state, so concurrent execution is a non-issue; the two stateful fakes are constructed per call and root vitest runs non-concurrently. The models do not defensively validate their own input shapes (a malformed J1Trace would throw rather than refuse) — they are typed models consumed by typed callers, and adding runtime shape guards would duplicate the contracts decoders. Store fault tests use in-memory ephemeral databases, so no file contention or cleanup path exists; withStore closes in a finally regardless.
